original_text: I wanted to reach out to discuss the opportunity to leverage my experience.
user_feedback: don't say 'leverage', say 'use'
expected_intent: Replace 'leverage' with 'use' in all professional writing

original_text: I genuinely believe this role aligns with my career trajectory.
user_feedback: drop 'genuinely' — it's AI slop
expected_intent: Never use 'genuinely' as an intensifier

original_text: The challenge isn't technical — it's organizational.
user_feedback: kill the negative parallelism, just say what it is
expected_intent: Never contrast what something isn't with what it is

original_text: I am writing to express my interest in the Senior PM position.
user_feedback: never start with 'I am writing to'
expected_intent: Never open a cover letter with 'I am writing to' or variants

original_text: Furthermore, my experience at DreamWorks demonstrates my ability to facilitate cross-functional alignment.
user_feedback: don't say 'furthermore' and don't say 'facilitate'
expected_intent: Never use 'furthermore' or 'facilitate' in prose

original_text: I believe my background makes me a strong fit for this position.
user_feedback: say 'I think' not 'I believe' — 'believe' is too formal
expected_intent: Use 'I think' instead of 'I believe' for hedging

original_text: This is a compelling opportunity to drive impact in the physical AI space.
user_feedback: too corporate, sounds like a press release
expected_intent: Avoid corporate-sounding phrases like 'drive impact' and 'compelling opportunity'

original_text: At DreamWorks, I spearheaded a product redesign initiative that culminated in a 15% improvement in user retention metrics.
user_feedback: way too formal — say 'led' not 'spearheaded', 'resulted in' not 'culminated in'
expected_intent: Use plain verbs (led, built, shipped) over inflated ones (spearheaded, culminated, orchestrated)

original_text: I would love to explore how my skills could contribute to your team's mission.
user_feedback: say 'I'd love to' not 'I would love to'
expected_intent: Use contractions in professional register — 'I'd' not 'I would'

original_text: Having worked extensively in product management for over a decade, I have developed a keen understanding of the challenges inherent in scaling operations.
user_feedback: that's one sentence and it's 30 words, split it
expected_intent: Hard cap of 30 words per sentence — split longer ones

original_text: I built the search tool. I led the redesign. I shipped the new API. I fixed the onboarding flow. I wrote the PRD.
user_feedback: five sentences in a row with the same structure, vary it
expected_intent: Never have 3+ consecutive sentences with similar structure or length

original_text: The product — which was built over six months — addressed three key challenges: onboarding friction — users couldn't find core features — latency — pages took 3s+ to load — and retention — 40% churned in week one.
user_feedback: way too many em dashes, max 2 per document
expected_intent: Maximum 2 em dashes per document, use periods or commas instead

original_text: Physical AI. The next frontier. Operators need tools. Not dashboards. Real tools.
user_feedback: no sentence fragments in prose — those aren't sentences
expected_intent: No sentence fragments in prose — every sentence needs a subject and verb

original_text: The most interesting thing about this space is that nobody is talking about the real problem, which I'll get into below.
user_feedback: cut the forward reference, just say the thing
expected_intent: No forward references like 'which I'll get into below' — just say it

original_text: Hey team, just wanted to circle back on the doc review — would love to get everyone's eyes on it before EOD Friday if possible, no rush though!
user_feedback: this is slack, be way shorter
expected_intent: Slack messages should be 1-2 sentences max — cut filler

original_text: Dear Hiring Manager, I am excited to submit my application for the Senior Product Manager position at your esteemed organization.
user_feedback: way too formal for a cover letter, drop 'Dear Hiring Manager' and 'esteemed organization'
expected_intent: Cover letters should use warm professional register, not formal — no 'Dear Hiring Manager' or 'esteemed'

original_text: I'm a product leader with deep expertise in AI-powered systems, and I'm passionate about building tools that empower operators to make data-driven decisions.
user_feedback: never say 'passionate about' or 'empower' — those are AI tells
expected_intent: Never use 'passionate about' or 'empower' — recognized AI writing tells

original_text: This role is the kind of challenge that excites me most.
user_feedback: 'the kind of X that' is AI slop — just say what excites you
expected_intent: Never use 'the kind of X that' pattern — AI writing tell

original_text: In my previous role, I collaborated with cross-functional stakeholders to align on strategic priorities and execute against ambitious OKRs.
user_feedback: this is buzzword soup — what did you actually DO
expected_intent: Use concrete outcomes over abstract process language — what shipped, what moved

original_text: I noticed your team is working on some really interesting problems in the logistics space.
user_feedback: 'really interesting' is vague — name the specific problem
expected_intent: Be specific about what interests you — name the problem, not 'interesting'
